newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Independent unit picks up 9.76 pct in bid for W&H.
newsitem.headline: Independent unit picks up 9.76 pct in bid for W&H.

text.p: Independent Press Communications Ltd, a subsidiary of Independent Newspapers Plc, said it had so far acquired 9.76 percent in its bid for New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton.
IPCL is bidding for all of Wilson and Horton, offering NZ$11.00 or 1.375 exchangeable INP shares for each W&H share.

Independent Newspapers and family trusts linked to principal Tony O'Reilly held 45.15 percent of Wilson and Horton prior to the bid. IPCL Chairman Michael Walls said the aggregate holding had therefore now risen to 54.91 percent.
"This is an unusually high acceptance rate at this early stage of the bid and reflects both the fairness of the bid and the attractiveness of the exchangeable shares," he said.

About 75 percent of acceptances to date have been for the exchangeable shares. This means that approximately 25 percent of the available exchangeable shares have now been secured by Wilson & Horton shareholders on a first-come-first-served basis.
IPCL said it was accelerating payments under its cash offer, so shareholders who opted for this would receive their NZ$11.00/share within seven days of acceptances being received.
